newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia army bans convoy of party supporters.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia army bans convoy of party supporters.

text.p: Indonesia's military said on Monday it would ban a motorised convoy planned for this month by supporters of the divided Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) from Java to Bali, the official Antara news agency reported.

The agency quoted Major-General Imam Utomo, head of the Brawijaya military command covering East Java, as saying he had agreed with the commander of the Udayana military command covering Bali to ban the convoy scheduled to start on Wednesday.

"We haven't got any direction from the armed forces commander. But we have agreed to ban the long march (convoy) because political activities are not supposed to be held now. They should be held during the election," Utomo was quoted as saying.

The supporters, who say their move is aimed at uniting the party, plan to stage a convoy of cars, which they bill as a "long march", from Bali to Jakarta passing through a number of large cities on Java including Surabaya, Yogyakarta and Bandung.
The convoy plans to cover the distance of 1,500 km (937 miles) in seven days.

The minority PDI split into two camps when a government-backed congress last June elected deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi to replace Megawati Sukarnoputri, daughter of Indonesia's first president, Sukarno.
Megawati's legal challenge to the congress is before the High Court.
One of the convoy organisers, who asked not to be named, told Reuters on Monday they planned to go ahead with the convoy despite the army's ban.
"We will go on. We expect people to join us from the cities we visit," she said, declining to say how many cars or people would take part in the convoy.
She said those taking part were "neutral" and not loyal to either Surjadi or Megawati.
Megawati's ouster has been strongly opposed by her supporters and rioting broke out in Jakarta last July after a police-backed takeover of the party's headquarters by Surjadi's supporters.
Five people died in the riots, the worst in the capital in two decades.
Soetjipto, chief of the faction of East Java's branch of the PDI under Megawati, said the party was not involved in the planned convoy. The general election is scheduled for May 29.
